Messages.Author: ramst...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
Hello,

What is the ruling on the following situation?

Player A announces Bleed on Player B.

Player B uses Rat's Warning to wake minion to block bleed action.

Player A plays Change of Target and cancels the bleed action.

Does Player B's minion go back to being tapped or does it stay awake?

Thanks

Michael Eichler

Sent via Deja.com http://www.deja.com/
Before you buy.

Messages.Author: Noal McDonald
Messages.Body:
ramst...@my-deja.com wrote:
> Player A announces Bleed on Player B.
> Player B uses Rat's Warning to wake minion to block bleed action.
> Player A plays Change of Target and cancels the bleed action.
> Does Player B's minion go back to being tapped or does it stay awake?

Unlike WWEF and Forced Awakening, Rats Warning and Guard Dogs explicitly
untaps the minion when a bleed action is announced. The vampire using
those cards is under no obligation to block.

So...to answer your question, Player B's minion stays untapped.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
ramst...@my-deja.com wrote:
>
> Hello,
>
> What is the ruling on the following situation?
>

> Player A announces Bleed on Player B.
>
> Player B uses Rat's Warning to wake minion to block bleed action.
>
> Player A plays Change of Target and cancels the bleed action.
>
> Does Player B's minion go back to being tapped or does it stay awake?

He remains untapped. "Awake" is a bad term since it implies things
like Wake with Evening's Freshness or Forced Awakening - neither of
which untap the reacting vampire.
